newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk minister demands chapel turned into mosque.
newsitem.headline: Turk minister demands chapel turned into mosque.

text.p: Turkey's Islamist minister of culture has demanded that a chapel in a popular western resort town be turned into a mosque, the town's mayor said on Thursday.
"I have seen some documents, sent by culture ministry, demanding action to turn a historic chapel in Bodrum castle into a small mosque," Bodrum's mayor, Tugrul Acar, told Reuters.

He said a minaret had already been built next to the 15th-century chapel after a previous decision. "But the current minister wants the chapel, which is now used for archaeological exhibitions, emptied and turned into a mosque," he added.
Ismail Kahraman, the culture minister of Turkey's caretaker Islamist-led government, has drawn strong media criticism because of his alleged anti-secularist rule at the ministry.
Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan resigned last week amid a row with the strongly secularist armed forces over the government's alleged encouragement of Islamic activism.
Erbakan, leader of the Islam-based Welfare Party, has stayed on as caretaker prime minister while secularist parties attempt to form a government.

"This is not Kahraman's decision, there was a previous plan to reconstruct the castle, including turning the chapel into a small mosque as it was under Ottoman rule," a Culture Ministry spokesman said.
But Acar said the reconstruction plan only included building the minaret. "Changing it into a mosque is something that the Welfare Party wants to do," he said.
Around 1,500 people in Bodrum, famed for its nightclubs, protested against the ministry's plan on Monday and vowed not to allow any change to the chapel, the Turkish daily, Sabah said.
